analysis: The code snippet calls filename.substring(index + 1). The method first checks if filename is null and returns null. Then it obtains the last index of '.' (index = filename.lastIndexOf(".")). If index < 0, it returns null. So only when index >= 0 and filename is non-null does the substring call execute. For substring, the only declared exception is IndexOutOfBoundsException when beginIndex is negative or larger than the string length. Since index >= 0, index+1 >= 1, so beginIndex is not negative. Also, because index is the last occurrence of '.', it must be <= filename.length()-1, so index+1 <= filename.length(). Therefore beginIndex is never larger than the length. Both conditions are fully avoided by the preceding checks.
remark: The throwing condition for IndexOutOfBoundsException requires beginIndex < 0 or beginIndex > length. Here, beginIndex = index+1, where index is the last index of '.' and is non-negative and <= length-1, so beginIndex is always between 1 and length inclusive. Thus, the exception cannot occur.
